coach.name: Jeff Boals
coach.notes: Ohio alumnus. Entered 2026-27 at 129-93 (.581) at Ohio, 73-51 (.589) in MAC play, 184-135 (.577) overall including Stony Brook. 2025-26 was his first sub-.500 season at Ohio (15-17, 9-9 MAC) and ended with a second straight first-round MAC Tournament loss (86-75 to Kent State); afterward he said 'We've got to be better, and there's going to be a reset,' took responsibility for accountability lapses, said the non-conference schedule was 'probably a little too difficult,' and promised to 'reset this program from a culture standpoint.' Only three of 12 scholarship players returned. No 2026 contract news found in coverage read.

storylines.headline: Culture reset after Boals' first losing season
storylines.detail: After a 15-17 year and an 86-75 MAC Tournament loss to Kent State, Boals promised a reset, admitted accountability failures (notably with Hadaway's technical fouls) and said the non-conference schedule was too hard; nine scholarship players left and the roster was rebuilt with transfers and three international players.

storylines.headline: Paveletzke's surprise fifth year
storylines.detail: Listed as departing in spring coverage, Jackson Paveletzke (17.3 PPG, 5.4 APG) returned for a fifth season of eligibility (wire headline via Crescent-News), was named Preseason All-MAC Second Team, and scored 20 in the opener. Per the wire story, the extra year comes from the NCAA's newly adopted age-based 'five-in-five' eligibility rule; he announced on social media 'I'm back,' calling it a 'victory lap.' He has started all 63 games across two seasons at Ohio.

storylines.headline: International trio: Brogan, Makitan, Ledegen
storylines.detail: Australian guard Ché Brogan (18 points in 12 minutes vs NC A&T), Bosnian forward Dusan Makitan (starter) and Belgian forward Siebe Ledegen (starter, EuroBasket 2025 experience) all played major roles in the first two games.

storylines.headline: Hometown return: Kyler D'Augustino
storylines.detail: Athens County native (Alexander HS, 2,000+ career points) transferred home from IU Indy after an 18.5 PPG All-Horizon Third Team season.

storylines.headline: 2-0 start; Purdue next
storylines.detail: Ohio beat South Alabama 86-77 (Mitchell career-high seven 3s) and NC A&T 80-70, then travels to Purdue on Nov 13 followed by New Mexico State in Jacksonville Nov 24.

storylines.headline: Defense is the question
storylines.detail: Mid-Major Madness framed the season around whether a high-scoring backcourt (Paveletzke, D'Augustino, Mitchell) can be paired with enough defense; Ohio ranked near the bottom of D-I in 3-point defense early in 2025-26 per the Athens Messenger.

recent_news.headline: Ohio fires from 3-point range, wins season opener 86-77 at South Alabama
recent_news.detail: Trailed 35-34 at half. Kolton Mitchell 21 points on a career-high seven 3s; Jackson Paveletzke 20 (all after halftime, 4-4 FT in final minute); contributions from Ledegen, Simmons (two dunks), Makitan, D'Augustino and Marin Petkov (two 3s).

recent_news.headline: Ohio staves off comeback, beats NC A&T 80-70 in home opener to move to 2-0
recent_news.detail: Fell behind 14-5, led 38-31 at half after a 33-17 run. Starters: Simmons, Paveletzke, Ledegen, Makitan, Mitchell. Freshman Ché Brogan scored 18 in 12 minutes off the bench. Boals: team was 'punched in the mouth' early but 'No one panicked.' Next: at Purdue (Nov 13).
